notes: Pattern across the products, from their own docs: (1) Amortizers — YNAB, Quicken (Windows and Mac), Moneydance, Banktivity — compute the interest portion from rate + current balance + payment (plus compounding period in Quicken/Banktivity, rounding method in Banktivity) and post it themselves; YNAB posts interest as a separate automatic charge in the loan account and records the payment as a plain transfer; Quicken/Moneydance/Banktivity record the payment as a split with principal transferred to the loan account and interest to an expense category. (2) Balance-only trackers — Monarch, Copilot, Empower, Simplifi — do not compute interest; the user restates the balance by hand (Monarch/Copilot/Empower) or hand-splits principal/interest and lets the balance be the transaction sum (Simplifi). (3) On disagreement with a stated balance: YNAB has an explicit 'Update Balance' flow that re-confirms the rate and posts a balance adjustment for the difference; Moneydance overwrites the Principal field to the lender's balance; Quicken Windows keeps balance-adjustment entries in the manual loan register and documents that rounding differences versus the lender are expected and small; Quicken Mac lets the user override the split by hand with the correction applied from the next payment; Copilot overwrites today's balance; Simplifi recomputes from transactions. All amortizers explicitly caveat that their interest may not match the lender's (Quicken: decimal places; Moneydance: 'slightly different methods'; YNAB: 'estimated' and user-editable per month, including past months). Lender transaction feeds are not relied on by any of them: YNAB, Quicken Windows and Simplifi each state linked loans deliver a balance but no payment transactions. Quote fidelity: all quotes were taken from page text fetched by curl or the Zendesk JSON API, except the Quicken Mac FAQ, Quicken 'make a loan payment', Moneydance 'Enter an Existing Loan', Simplifi and Copilot quotes, which are the fragments WebFetch returned verbatim from those pages.

The CMHC indemnity PDF was text-extracted with pdfminer. Key takeaways for the app: (1) the Canadian mortgage periodic rate for a monthly payment is i = (1 + r/2)^(1/6) − 1 (CMHC), with the payment from the standard annuity formula on the remaining amortization; the Interest Act requires the rate to be stated yearly or half-yearly not in advance and caps charges at the stated rate; (2) lines of credit: variable prime-based rate, interest on the daily balance from the withdrawal date, no grace period, minimum payment typically the month's interest (FCAC); (3) credit cards: no interest on purchases when the balance is paid in full by a due date at least 21 days after the cycle end (Bank Act s. 627.34), otherwise interest on the (average) daily balance charged on the last day of the cycle, with cash advances and balance transfers accruing from the transaction date; payments above the minimum allocated highest-rate-first or pro rata (s. 627.35). The Cost of Borrowing (Banks) Regulations were repealed in 2022; cite SOR/2021-181 instead. The relayed user remark about matching activity data to external accounts is outside this research sub-task and was not acted on here.
